solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Anti-war literary genre getting no opening in time gone by

indicators.note: the shortened genre goes inside the word for time gone by

parts.note: the past is time gone by

indicators.note: the genre's name loses its first letter, its opening

parts.note: sci-fi, science fiction, is a literary genre

explanation.surface: A reader rejects war stories and longs for an old-fashioned kind of book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Anti-war' looks like a description of the genre, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone opposed to all war is a pacifist; here the adjective sense, opposed to fighting, fits.

clue.text: Stone with hard core

parts.note: the pit of a fruit is its stone
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A fruit stone with a hard centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Pith is the essential centre or heart of something, its core.

clue.text: Loss of power after Liberal has infiltrated religious group

indicators.note: has got inside, so the letter goes into the middle of the word

parts.note: a power cut is a loss of electricity, so cut

explanation.surface: A sect loses its influence once a Liberal has worked their way inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has infiltrated' places L inside CUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A cult is a small religious sect, often with a devoted following.

clue.text: American unfavourably engaged in diminishing gunfire

indicators.note: held within, so the two short pieces go inside the word for diminishing

parts.note: to fade is to diminish
ill means badly, unfavourably, as in think ill of

explanation.surface: An American is caught in fading gunfire, to their disadvantage.
explanation.definitionFit: A fusillade is a burst of many guns firing together, a volley of gunfire.

clue.text: Newspaper is source of coupons in footwear and bedding

indicators.note: the picked letter goes inside the footwear

parts.note: a sandal is an item of footwear

indicators.note: the first letter is where the word starts, its source

parts.note: a sheet is bedding

explanation.surface: A newspaper is where you find coupons, among adverts for shoes and bedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'source of' takes the C of coupons, which 'in' puts into SANDAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A gossip paper that trades in shocking stories is a lurid kind of tabloid newspaper.

clue.text: Understood one in church recalled architectural style

parts.note: 'got it' means understood it

indicators.note: called back, so the pair of church letters around one is read backwards
the letter for one sits inside the church abbreviation

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone grasped what a church guide recalled about a building's style.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversal covers the church letters with one inside them, not the word for understood.
explanation.definitionFit: Gothic is the medieval European building style of pointed arches and rib vaults.

clue.text: Old doctor disposing of new instruments

indicators.note: getting rid of, so the letter is dropped

parts.note: Bones is slang for a doctor, as in Star Trek's Dr McCoy

explanation.surface: An old doctor gets rid of some new instruments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposing of' drops the N from BONES, leaving BOES.
explanation.definitionFit: Oboes are double-reed woodwind instruments of the orchestra.

clue.text: A graduate in Northern city with facilities to make a racket

indicators.note: being in the city means the graduate's letters follow straight on from its name

parts.note: Hull is a city in the north of England
a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate
loo is British slang for the toilet, the facilities

explanation.surface: A graduate in a northern English city uses the toilets to make noise.
explanation.walkthrough: Hull is a port city in Yorkshire; 'loo' is the everyday British word for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: A hullabaloo is a noisy commotion, so a racket in the sense of din.

clue.text: Fruit, very pleasant during middle of break

parts.note: clement weather is mild and very pleasant
in means during, as in 'in the morning'

indicators.note: the centre letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: Fruit is a lovely snack during the middle of a work break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle of' takes the E at the centre of BREAK.
explanation.definitionFit: A clementine is a small citrus fruit, a variety of mandarin orange.

clue.text: Charm is maintained in most of chat with a guy

indicators.note: held inside, so the little word goes into the middle of the rest
only most of the word is used, its last letter dropped

parts.note: to talk is to chat
a man is a guy

explanation.surface: Charm is kept up in most conversations with a man.
explanation.definitionFit: A talisman is a lucky charm, an object thought to bring good fortune.

clue.text: Soccer player: "Try a position"

parts.note: to have a go is to try
the lie of something is its position, as in the lie of the land

explanation.surface: A footballer is told to try playing in a certain spot.
explanation.walkthrough: In golf the lie is where the ball comes to rest, a sense of position worth knowing.
explanation.definitionFit: A goalkeeper in football is informally called a goalie.

clue.text: Reserve about Northern mood? Article shows lack of restraint

indicators.note: around, so the reserve word wraps the rest

parts.note: ice is coldness of manner, reserve
a temper is a mood, as in a good temper
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A reticent manner in a northern mood is contrasted with an article on excess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reserve' here is a cool, aloof manner, not something kept back.
explanation.definitionFit: Intemperance is excess, especially in drinking, and so a lack of self-restraint.

clue.text: Variable assessment of trombone music?

definitions.meaning: a scale of charges or payments that changes with circumstances, such as income
a trombone moves by sliding, so a scale played on it could be called a sliding one

explanation.surface: A music critic grades a trombone performance in a changeable way.
explanation.definitionFit: A scale of fees that rises or falls with income is a variable assessment; the trombone's slide gives the playful reading.

clue.text: It's to be involved with pledge and a bit of commitment?

definitions.text: It's to be involved with pledge and a bit of commitment?

indicators.note: tangled together, so these letters are mixed into a new order
just a small piece, the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Marriage is about getting tied up with vows and a little dedication.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' mixes ITS, PLEDGE and the C from 'a bit of commitment'; the whole clue also describes marrying.
explanation.definitionFit: To get spliced is British slang for to get married, which means making a pledge of commitment.

clue.text: Shattering rocks put in alignment?

indicators.note: rocks as a verb, shakes, so the word's letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Shattering rocks set something in order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocks' is the anagram signal, not a noun; the definition is a whimsical way to say level or line up.
explanation.definitionFit: To make something straight is to bring it into line, so to put it in alignment.

clue.text: No great contribution to film run

definitions.meaning: a background actor in a crowd scene makes only a small contribution to a film
in cricket, a bye or wide is a run not scored off the bat, called by this name

explanation.surface: A minor film part is said to have run on.
explanation.definitionFit: A film walk-on and a cricket bye or wide share the name; in cricket, runs not scored by the batter go into a separate tally.

clue.text: Plan to attack fake story I want amended, after taking in newspaper

indicators.note: the assembled letters take the newspaper's letter inside them

parts.note: a lie is a made-up story

indicators.note: changed, so the letters of these two words are rearranged

parts.note: the i is a British national newspaper

explanation.surface: An editor plans to attack a fake story, wanting it corrected after a newspaper takes it on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amended' turns I WANT into INWAT; 'after taking in' adds the I of the i newspaper inside, before the T.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie in wait is to hide ready to ambush someone, a plan to attack.

clue.text: No Communist to occupy flat in Parisian building

indicators.note: the Communist moves in, so the word sits inside the flat word

parts.note: tame means dull, flat
a red is a Communist

explanation.surface: Communists are not allowed to take over flats in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' is the adjective, dull, not an apartment.
explanation.definitionFit: Notre-Dame is the Gothic cathedral on the Ile de la Cité in Paris.

clue.text: Expedition on board trendy craft going far?

indicators.note: on board, read as inside the ship, so the speed word sits within it

parts.note: being on board means being on a ship, and steamship is abbreviated in crosswords to two letters
expedition here means speed, the older sense of being expeditious, so pace
hip means fashionable, trendy

explanation.surface: A speedy trip on a fashionable boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' is the crossword convention of going inside SS, the steamship abbreviation; 'Expedition' means haste, not a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: A rocket craft built for journeys beyond Earth travels very far, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Name assigned to god is a problematic point

parts.note: Thor is the Norse god of thunder

explanation.surface: A name is given to a deity, and that turns out to be a sticking point.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorn is a sharp spike on a plant, and figuratively a persistent nuisance.

clue.text: Cheerful illumination requiring attention — skill to be brought in

parts.note: light is illumination

indicators.note: the skill word is put inside the attention word

parts.note: to pay heed is to pay attention
art is skill, as in the art of persuasion

explanation.surface: Bright lighting needs careful attention and skill in its design.
explanation.definitionFit: Being carefree and happy is the meaning of this compound adjective, a synonym of cheerful.

clue.text: Bunk with sheet finally on ready

indicators.note: the last letter of the word is taken

parts.note: ripe fruit is ready to eat

explanation.surface: A bed with a sheet, finally made up and ready.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bunk' looks like a bed, but it means nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Bunk and tripe both mean nonsense, rubbish talk.

clue.text: European to allow twice the time

parts.note: to let is to allow
T is the abbreviation for time; 'twice' says a second T follows the one already ending the allow word

explanation.surface: A European is allowed double time.
explanation.walkthrough: The word for allow already ends in T, so 'twice the time' means one more T.
explanation.definitionFit: A Lett is a native of Latvia, so a European.

clue.text: Charge up, snatching one item

indicators.note: grabbing hold of, so the letter is taken inside
in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: a rap is a criminal charge, as in a murder rap
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A charge goes up as a single item is stolen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns RAP to PAR, and 'snatching' takes I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A couple in a relationship are said to be an item, so a pair.

clue.text: What may be related to Siamese flower spike

parts.note: a Siamese is a breed of cat
kin are relatives, so related people are kin

explanation.surface: A question about what a Siamese might be related to.
explanation.walkthrough: Whimsically, relatives of a Siamese cat would be cat kin.
explanation.definitionFit: A catkin is the dangling spike of tiny flowers on willow, hazel or birch.

clue.text: American punished without full scrutiny?

indicators.note: roughly handled, so the letters of the word are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: An American is penalised without a full investigation.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is playful: a hearing in private escapes public scrutiny.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial held in private, behind closed doors, is out of public view; the Latin legal phrase means 'in chamber'.

clue.text: Risk pulling line from hanging item

indicators.note: pulling out, so the line letter is removed

parts.note: a dangler is something that hangs down

explanation.surface: It is risky to pull a line from something hanging.
explanation.definitionFit: Danger and risk are synonyms: both mean exposure to possible harm.

clue.text: Second church festival engages me for a study period

indicators.note: takes on a replacement: the festival swaps one of its letters for the little word

parts.note: Easter is the main Christian festival
taken as written

explanation.surface: A second church celebration hires the speaker for a term of study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engages' here means taking on a stand-in: the festival's A is replaced, not just added to.
explanation.definitionFit: A semester is one of the two terms of a university year, a period of study.
